A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Modeling Saliency Dataset Bias and provide readable methods, equations, results, figures and appendices. Added material and relocated or renumbered content can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original saliency-model evaluations, cross-dataset adaptation experiments, ablations and case analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds comparator evaluations and expanded multiscale and computational-cost results.

M1.justification: Both versions use CLIP/DINOv2 multiscale features, the same readout network and interpretable dataset-specific bias parameters. v2 explicitly describes feature concatenation and formalizes the prediction pipeline; these clarify the existing method rather than establish procedural changes.

E1.justification: Both cover MIT1003, CAT2000, COCO-Freeview, DAEMONS and FIGRIM, with SALICON pretraining and additional MIT300, Kienzle, Toronto and SALICON evaluations. The additional-dataset experiments in v2 Appendix D were already present in v1 Appendix C.

E2.justification: v2 substantially broadens comparisons: Table 6 adds Itti & Koch, RARE2012, GBVS and CovSal across five datasets; benchmark tables add TempSAL, and MIT300 Table 3 adds SalTR and GSGNet. Table 2 also adds EML-NET participation on CAT2000 and COCO-Freeview and SalFBNet on CAT2000.

E3.justification: The main splits, preprocessing, metrics and training schedules remain unchanged. The revised multiscale experiment introduces absolute-only, relative-only and combined configurations, one to five scales per type, small-first versus large-first scale selection, and epoch-time measurement.

E4.justification: v1 Appendix E/Figure 12 compares scale counts and dataset-specific versus shared scale weights. v2 Appendix F/Figure 11 replaces this with broader scale-family, resolution-selection and computational-cost analyses, without retaining the separate weight-sharing curves. Other ablations, sensitivity tests and case studies remain.

E5.justification: Both retain paired-comparison error bars, variability across random adaptation subsets, and 95% intervals for centerbias experiments. Dataset-parameter plots retain bootstrapped 95% confidence intervals across four random seeds. No changed run counts or uncertainty-estimation procedures are reported.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial comparator-result blocks and new multiscale/runtime curves while retaining Table 1 and existing proposed-model benchmark scores. For example, new Table 6 reports CAT2000 AUCs of 0.847 for CovSal, 0.802 for GBVS and 0.777 for RARE2012, versus the retained EML-NET result of 0.766. These are additional results, not improved scores for the proposed model.

T1.justification: v2 Appendix H expresses the existing rescaling, weighted averaging, readout and probability-map construction in equations. This is a formal restatement rather than new mathematical reasoning, a derivation or a proof. The information-gain definition is unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction refines the stated generalization-gap closure from about 80% to about 75%, aligning it with the retained 76% result and existing contribution language. The central dataset-bias, parameter-efficiency, data-efficiency and benchmark-leadership claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 Appendix F adds practical guidance that fewer high-resolution scales, preferably relative scales, offer acceptable computational tradeoffs at a few percent performance cost. Existing interpretations of dataset bias, failure cases, applicability boundaries and imperfect gold-standard estimates are retained.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents backbone-feature concatenation, normalized nonnegative scale weights and the full prediction equation, and adds per-epoch timing measurements. Existing backbone layers, resolutions, optimizer settings, learning-rate schedules, hardware and code/data access information remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds seven references and brief coverage of temporal prediction, diffusion augmentation, transformer methods, global semantic guidance, self-distillation and CovSal. The existing positioning relative to DeepGaze and dataset adaptation is largely retained.

P1.justification: Targeted edits reorganize the model explanation into a separate Pretrained Backbones paragraph, add Appendix B and a mathematical-formulation paragraph, and revise the multiscale discussion. Author-name, acknowledgment and cross-reference edits accompany these changes; most prose and section ordering remain.

P2.justification: v2 adds an enlarged architecture diagram as Figure 9 and an extended comparison table as Table 6, expands benchmark tables, and replaces the single multiscale plot with three panels. Several figures are resized and appendix material reflows. Figure 11 unfortunately retains a caption describing the old weight-sharing comparison.

improvement.justification: Broader baseline comparisons and the expanded scale/compute analysis improve evidential coverage and practical guidance. The enlarged architecture diagram and explicit computation description also help readers inspect the method. These are limited gains to an already developed study; loss of the separate weight-sharing ablation and Figure 11's mismatched caption partially offset them.
